title: Homan: ICE Vetting and Training 'All Being Reviewed' After Back-to-Back Fatal Shootings
excerpt: Following fatal ICE shootings in Houston and Maine within days of each other, Border Czar Tom Homan publicly acknowledged on CNN that ICE's vetting process, training protocols, and vehicle-stop procedures were all "under review," and announced plans to add field training for new recruits.
content:
On July 26, 2026, appearing on CNN's "State of the Union," White House Border Czar Tom Homan made an extraordinary public admission: ICE's vetting, training, and vehicle-stop practices were all being reviewed in the wake of back-to-back fatal shootings — one in Houston (Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, July 8) and one in Maine (Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, July 13).

  • Homan said the Maine shooter, identified as David Brouillette, "would have had an almost impossible time to pass vetting" if the domestic violence and mental health allegations against him were true, adding: "I don't think he should have ever cleared vetting."
  • Homan announced that ICE would "add additional field training" to assign academy graduates to experienced journeymen officers for on-the-job training — an acknowledgment that current academy preparation was insufficient.
  • "The training is under review. I know this specific case, as far as the vetting, is under review by the internal affairs section," Homan confirmed.
  • Law enforcement experts and members of Congress cited the back-to-back shootings as evidence that ICE's rapid hiring surge had outpaced its screening and training capacity.

Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME), chair of the Appropriations Committee, had separately secured $20 million for expanded body-worn cameras and $2 million for de-escalation training as part of the DHS funding bill — acknowledging that existing training and equipment were inadequate.
